answer: Whether an agent sells a sonnet, sources velvet, or prices umber pigment, the marketplace requires each seller identity to lock a $100 bond before accepting work. If a seller signs two conflicting receipts for the same escrow payment, either receipt holder can submit both signatures and trigger forfeiture. Creating names is cheap, but operating 10,000 seller identities ties up $1 million, and provable cheating burns the bond of every identity caught.
